name: Milk collection centres and chillers

problems.words: Fat readings are written by hand and farmers argue every payday
quick_ideas: Give each supplier a slip with litres and readings at every delivery
Take the reading in front of the supplier so there's nothing to doubt later.

workzap_build.text: credit_ledger — each delivery entered at intake, with a WhatsApp slip sent to the supplier (with their permission) and weekly statements built without manual effort.

problems.ask_first: What's tested when milk arrives today?
problems.free_stops: The intake entry, slip and statement setup go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many payday arguments come from each writer's register this week, so you see where handwritten records create the most trouble.
Give one person the job of checking every day's handwritten readings before filing, so payday disputes are easier to settle from the register.

problems.words: Suppliers say our test is wrong and move to another chiller
quick_ideas: Keep a weekly list of active suppliers so anyone who stops shows up
Ask those who left, politely, what made them go.

workzap_build.text: supplier activity tracked daily, with suppliers who've dropped off flagged right away.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many suppliers deliver to you?
problems.free_stops: When a supplier counts as dropped and the follow-up flow stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which collection shift each departing supplier last used this week, so you can spot whether trust is breaking at a particular handover.
Give one person the job of marking every supplier who stops delivering on one notebook page, so losses are noticed before routes thin out.

problems.words: Plant rejected a whole tanker and deducted it from our payment
quick_ideas: Get every rejection in writing with the reason
Note which routes' milk went into that tanker so problems can be traced.

workzap_build.text: each tanker's load, sources, seal photo and plant result logged, with rejections linked back to routes without manual work.

problems.ask_first: Does the plant give you the rejection reason in writing?
problems.free_stops: How loads are traced back to routes is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare tanker rejections with the centres and routes feeding them that day, so you can see where deductions are starting.
Give one person the job of keeping every plant rejection note in one folder, so deduction reasons are easy to trace later.

problems.words: Litres collected don't match litres dispatched
quick_ideas: Total intake and dispatch at the same time every day
Look for which centre or shift the gap comes from.

workzap_build.text: daily_reports — collected vs dispatched reconciled without extra work by day and centre.

problems.ask_first: Where do you think the gap happens?
problems.free_stops: The reconciliation rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write intake and dispatch totals beside each shift for one week, so you can see whether the mismatch starts before loading or after.
Give one person the job of closing both intake and dispatch counts together daily, so the mismatch is checked before papers scatter.

problems.words: Advances to farmers aren't tracked properly, some never repay
quick_ideas: Write each advance and its agreed repayment in one register
Show the remaining balance on every payment slip.

workzap_build.text: an advance ledger per supplier that deducts repayments from each payout on its own.

problems.ask_first: How many suppliers have advances right now?
problems.free_stops: The deduction rules and ledger layout stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many repayment deductions were missed at payout this week, so you see how much weak tracking is costing.
Give one cashier the job of updating every advance balance in one register at payout, so unpaid amounts stop drifting between pages.

problems.words: We pay suppliers weekly but the plant pays us monthly
quick_ideas: Map out the next few weeks' money in and money out by date
Talk to your accountant before taking any finance to bridge the gap.

workzap_build.text: a running view of cash due in and out by date, updated daily from intake and buyer records.

problems.ask_first: Is the plant your only buyer?
problems.free_stops: How the cash view is built goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark each supplier payout day and each plant receipt day on one wall calendar this month, so your longest squeeze period stands out.
Give one office person a single notebook page for this week's promised payouts and expected plant receipts, so everyone checks the same place before committing cash.

problems.words: Cash payments to 300 farmers on one day is a risk
quick_ideas: Offer bank or wallet payment to suppliers willing to use it
Spread payouts across days by route.

workzap_build.text: every payout recorded by route and method, with cash out checked against statements on its own.

problems.ask_first: How are most suppliers paid now?
problems.free_stops: The payout schedule and checks are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many payout slips are handed over in each hour on payment day, so you see when the office and cash table are under most strain.
Give one senior staff member the job of handing each route's payment bundle to the cashier at a fixed time, so the cash table stays calmer and less exposed.

problems.words: Generator broke and milk in the chiller turned
quick_ideas: Check the generator starts every day
Note every outage and any milk lost.

workzap_build.text: a generator and chiller log with downtime and diesel use, flagged to the owner the same day.

problems.ask_first: How often does the chiller lose power?
problems.free_stops: The log and flag rules stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every hour the generator was unavailable and whether the chiller was loaded, so you see when breakdowns hurt milk most.
Give one operator the job of logging generator stoppages in one notebook by date, so repeat downtime patterns are easier to spot.

problems.words: Driver may be skimming milk on the way
quick_ideas: Record litres loaded and seal number at every departure
Compare with the plant's receipt every day, openly.

workzap_build.text: a dispatch log with litres, seal photo and times, matched to the plant receipt right away.

problems.ask_first: Who drives the tanker, and how do you know when it leaves and arrives?
problems.free_stops: The dispatch log and matching rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare litres loaded, litres received and the same driver's route for each trip this week, so any recurring shortfall ties to a run.
Give one person the job of writing departure and receipt figures on the same page for every trip, so route shortfalls are harder to hide.

problems.words: Can't see daily intake across my 5 centres
quick_ideas: Ask each centre for the same few numbers every day
Put them side by side once a week.

workzap_build.text: a morning summary read across all centres with litres, average readings, active suppliers and cash due in and out.

problems.ask_first: How do the centres report to you now?
problems.free_stops: Which numbers go in and how centres are compared is worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each centre's intake on one page at closing for one week, so low-volume days and centres stand out clearly.
Give one staff member the job of collecting every centre's closing numbers before night, so daily intake stops arriving in mixed formats.

never_say: Anything about testing methods, preservatives or chemicals, or how to pass a quality check.
Anything that helps mask adulteration or tamper with tests, readings or tankers.
Anything that arranges or hides bribery of testing staff.
Collecting farmers' names, CNICs, phone or bank numbers into pi's own notes.

sample_reply.person: Okara ke paas chiller hai, roz 6,000 litre aata hai, aur har hafte farmers fat ki reading pe lad padte hain. Koi tareeqa?
sample_reply.pi:
Ji haan, ye theek ho sakta hai, aur is ke liye bade kharch ki zaroorat nahi.
Pehle, har delivery pe supplier ko litre aur reading wali aik parchi dein.
Doosra, reading supplier ke saamne li jaye, taake baad mein shak ki gunjaish na rahe.
Is ka pakka hal Workzap ye bana sakta hai: har delivery darj ho, supplier ko unki ijazat se WhatsApp pe foran slip mile, aur hafte ki statement khud ban jaye.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
